=== DOCS VERIFICATION (2026-06-08) ===
• trino.io/docs/current/sql/select.html — output column aliases (defined in the SELECT clause) are visible ONLY in the outer ORDER BY. The SQL-standard pre-projection-scope rule that bans referencing a SELECT alias in WHERE / GROUP BY / HAVING ALSO bans referencing it inside a SIBLING SELECT-list expression. Issue trinodb/trino #16533 confirms aliases not usable in GROUP BY (still open).
• trino.io/docs/current/functions/aggregate.html + GitHub issue trinodb/trino #7885 — `DISTINCT in window function parameters not yet supported`. `array_agg(DISTINCT ...) OVER (...)` and `count(DISTINCT col) OVER (PARTITION BY ...)` both error with this message. Issue still open.
• trino.io/docs/current/functions/array.html — Trino arrays are 1-based, verbatim: 'The [] operator is used to access an element of an array and is indexed starting from one'. element_at(arr, 0) is invalid (returns NULL via element_at or raises 'SQL array indices start at 1' via subscript). width_bucket CAN return 0 (the underflow bin), so DO NOT index a label array by the raw width_bucket result.
• trino.io/docs/current/functions/math.html — width_bucket has BOTH overloads; an N-element bounds array produces N+1 buckets (0..N). bucket 0 = below first bound (underflow); bucket N = at/above last bound (overflow/top). (Source-verified at the existing r07:2296-2301 lock — kept intact.)
• Integer-division floor: `floor(x/N)*N` is the docs-safest canonical (floor returns largest integer <= x; works for any sign). `CAST(x/N AS integer)*N` truncates TOWARD ZERO, not toward negative infinity — equivalent to floor for non-negative values only.
